rows.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
rows.subtopic: Electronic Configurations of Elements and the Periodic Table
rows.text: If an element with \(Z = 120\) is discovered, then which group of elements will it belong to?
Which one of the following statements is correct about \(\mathrm{N_2}\), CO, and \(\mathrm{NO^+}\)?
options: These are isoelectronic and have identical bond order.
These are isoelectronic and have different bond orders.
These are not isoelectronic but have identical bond order.
These are neither isoelectronic nor have identical bond order.

rows.text:
Which of the following complexes exhibit(s) magnetic moment close to 2 Bohr Magneton?

\(\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6](NO_3)_2}\), \(\mathrm{K_2[MnCl_4]}\), \(\mathrm{K_4[Mn(CN)_6]}\), and \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}\)

rows.subtopic: The Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) Theory
rows.text: According to the VSEPR theory, what are the most stable shapes of \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\) and \(\mathrm{SF_4}\), respectively?

The following complex ions absorb in the ultraviolet-visible region of light. Which one of these shows violet colour?

\(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]^{2+}}\), \(\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)(NH_3)_5]^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\), and \(\mathrm{[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}}\)

rows.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
rows.text: What is the relationship between the structures depicted below?

figure.note: Two sawhorse projections, each of two bonded carbons (lower-left carbon and upper-right carbon). Left structure: lower carbon bears H (left), CH3 (right) and OH (down); upper carbon bears F (up), H (left) and H (right). Right structure: lower carbon bears HO (left), H (right) and CH3 (down); upper carbon bears H (up), F (left) and H (right).

rows.text:
What is the correct order of acidity for the following compounds?

**M**: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}\)

**N**: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CO_2H}\)

**P**: \(\mathrm{2,4,6\text{-}(O_2N)_3C_6H_2OH}\)

**Q**: \(\mathrm{4\text{-}O_2NC_6H_4OH}\)

What are the products **N** and **Q** in the following reaction sequences?

\(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_3PO_2,\ H_2O}} \mathbf{M} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{anhyd.\ AlCl_3}]{\mathrm{CO,\ HCl}} \mathbf{N}\)

\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CN} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{SnCl_2,\ HCl}} \mathbf{P} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_3O^+}} \mathbf{Q}\)

rows.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
rows.text:
What are **X** and **Z** in the following sequence of reactions?

\(\mathbf{X} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{warm}]{\mathrm{HgSO_4,\ dil.\ H_2SO_4,\ H_2O}} \mathbf{Y} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{dil.\ NaOH,\ heat}]{\mathbf{Z}} \mathrm{PhCH{=}CHCOCH_3}\)
What are the correct structural descriptions for **M** and **N**?

figure.note: Two Haworth projections. M: six-membered ring with the ring O at top right. Ring carbon left of the O bears CH2OH (HO-CH2, up) and H (down); next carbon (left) bears H up and HO down; next (front left) bears OH up and H down; next (front right) bears H up and OH down; the carbon right of the ring O bears H up and OH down. N: five-membered ring with the ring O at top. Ring carbon left of the O bears CH2OH (HO-CH2, up) and H (down); next (front left) bears H up and OH down; next (front right) bears HO up and H down; the carbon right of the ring O bears OH up and CH2OH (down).

rows.text:
Consider an exothermic reaction:

\(\mathrm{2A(s) \longrightarrow B(s) + C(g) + D(g)}\)

The correct statement about the reaction is
options: spontaneous only at very high temperatures.
spontaneous only at very low temperatures.

rows.subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
rows.text:
The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from a metal corresponds to a wavelength of 500 nm. What is the total kinetic energy of all the photoelectrons ejected per second when the entire radiation from a 100 Watt bulb with a wavelength of 300 nm falls on the surface of the metal?

Planck's constant \(= 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\ s}\); speed of light \(= 3 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\ s^{-1}}\)

For a reaction \(\mathrm{R} \longrightarrow \mathrm{P}\) with a rate constant of \(3 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}\ s^{-1}}\), which one of the following plots is correct?

(Given \(\mathrm{[R]_0}\) is the initial concentration of R and [R] is the concentration of R at time t)
options: Plot of [R] against t: a straight line falling from near the top of the [R] axis
Plot of [R] against t: a curve falling steeply from the [R] axis and levelling off towards the t axis
Plot of \(\ln[\mathrm{R}]\) against t: a straight line falling from near the top of the axis
Plot of \(\log\left(\frac{[\mathrm{R}]_0}{[\mathrm{R}]}\right)\) against t: a straight line rising from the origin

rows.subtopic: Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass
rows.text: Which one of the following plots correctly describes the variation of osmotic pressure \((\Pi)\) of a fixed amount of a solute against the volume (V) of the solution at a fixed temperature?
options: Plot of \(\Pi\) against V from (0,0): a curve falling very steeply close to the \(\Pi\) axis, then flattening just above the V axis
Plot of \(\Pi\) against V from (0,0): a curve starting on the \(\Pi\) axis and falling more gradually, flattening just above the V axis
Plot of \(\Pi\) against V from (0,0): a straight line rising, starting just above and right of the origin
Plot of \(\Pi\) against V from (0,0): a straight line falling towards the V axis
